features.title: Friendly
features.description: Never used a unit test framework before? No problem! hTest is designed to be as friendly as possible to newcomers.

features.title: Declarative
features.description: Write your tests as nested object literals, with nice, readable syntax.

features.title: Flexible
features.description: You decide where your tests live, across how many files, and how they’re grouped. Anything you can `import`, you can test.

features.title: Boilerplate-free
features.description: Any commonalities between tests only specified once on the parent, and inherited. Anything that can be optional, is.

features.title: Quick to write
features.description: Most tests only need two properties: `args` and `expect`. No more excuses for not testing your utility functions!

features.title: ESM-first
features.description: Written in ESM from the get-go.

features.title: CLI and browser
features.description: Run your tests in the command line, in the browser, or both.

features.title: CI-ready
features.description: Fully compatible with continuous integration and automated test running processes.

features.title: Jump to source
features.description: Open a failing test's source file directly from the interactive CLI.

features.title: Watch mode
features.description: Tests re-run automatically when source files change. No manual restart needed.

features.title: Configurable
features.description: Use a config file for setup scripts, CLI flags, and shared options across your test suite.

features.title: Optional HTML-first mode
features.description: Working on UI-heavy code? Write tests in HTML, with reactive evaluation and mock interactions!

features.title: AI-agent friendly
features.description: Ships with a [`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md) reference for AI coding agents — teach Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, and others to write hTest tests correctly.
